chunks: And it is narrated from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who bought from another man a known amount of land for one hundred kurr, on condition that he would give him from the land. So he said: “It is forbidden.”
I said: “May I be your ransom, then if he buys the land from him for a known measure and wheat from other than it?” He said: “There is no harm in that.”

key_terms.أَرْضًا: land being sold in the transaction
key_terms.بِكَيْلٍ مَعْلُومٍ: by a known measured quantity, indicating contractual clarity
key_terms.بِمِائَةِ كُرٍّ: for one hundred kurr as a defined amount of payment
key_terms.جُرْبَانًا: a specified land measure or number of plots
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: legally forbidden in this form of sale
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ: there is no legal problem with that arrangement

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy land in exchange for produce from that same land?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the sale of land when payment is tied to produce from that same land. The Imam عليه السلام forbids such a transaction, while permitting the purchase when the payment is a known measure of wheat from another source. It highlights the importance of clear and valid sale terms in financial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3878 - It is narrated from Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Washsha' who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who purchased a specified number of plots of land from another man for one hundred kurr, with the condition that he would give him the payment from the yield of the land.
Imam (as) said: "This is forbidden."

I said: "May I be your ransom, what if he purchases the land with a specified measure and with wheat from elsewhere?"
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that."
